Study the table showing the production of four crops (in thousand tonnes) across five states and answer the question.

State | Rice | Wheat | Maize | Pulses
Punjab | 120 | 450 | 80 | 30
Haryana | 90 | 310 | 70 | 40
Uttar Pradesh | 350 | 380 | 150 | 120
Madhya Pradesh | 150 | 220 | 250 | 280
West Bengal | 400 | 50 | 60 | 90

Q. What is the average production of Wheat per state across the five given states?
explanation: Wheat production across the 5 states: Punjab (450) + Haryana (310) + Uttar Pradesh (380) + Madhya Pradesh (220) + West Bengal (50) = 1410 thousand tonnes. Average = 1410 / 5 = 282 thousand tonnes. Option B is correct. Option C or D are distractors from incorrect additions.

Q. Pulses production in Madhya Pradesh is approximately what percentage of the total pulses production across all five states?
explanation: Pulses production in Madhya Pradesh = 280 thousand tonnes. Total pulses production = 30 (Punjab) + 40 (Haryana) + 120 (Uttar Pradesh) + 280 (Madhya Pradesh) + 90 (West Bengal) = 600 thousand tonnes. Percentage = (280 / 600) * 100 = 46.67%. Option A is correct. Option C or B are incorrect calculations.

Q. मध्य प्रदेश में दालों का उत्पादन सभी पाँच राज्यों में कुल दाल उत्पादन का लगभग कितना प्रतिशत है?
explanation_hi: मध्य प्रदेश में दालों का उत्पादन = 280 हजार टन। सभी पाँच राज्यों में कुल दाल उत्पादन = 30 + 40 + 120 + 280 + 90 = 600 हजार टन। प्रतिशत = (280 / 600) × 100 = 46.67%。 अतः विकल्प A सही है।

Q. For Commerce faculty, what is the percentage increase in student enrollment from 2020 to 2024?
explanation: Enrollment in Commerce in 2020 was 60 and in 2024 was 100. Percentage increase = ((100 - 60) / 60) * 100 = (40 / 60) * 100 = 66.67%. Option B miscalculates the base value.

question:
Study the table below representing the percentage share of monthly expenditure heads of a family budget and answer the question.

Monthly Expenditure Heads (Pie-Chart Share)
Expenditure Head | Percentage Share (%) | Central Angle (Degrees)
Food | 40% | 144°
Rent | 25% | 90°
Education | 15% | 54°
Savings | 10% | 36°
Miscellaneous | 10% | 36°

Q. What is the ratio of the central angle for Food to the central angle for Savings?
explanation: Central angle for Food = 144°, and for Savings = 36°. Ratio = 144 / 36 = 4 / 1 = 4 : 1 (or equivalently, ratio of percentages 40% : 10% = 4 : 1). Option C is incorrect.
question_hi:
नीचे दी गई तालिका का अध्ययन करें जो एक परिवार के बजट के मासिक व्यय मदों के प्रतिशत हिस्से को दर्शाती है और प्रश्न का उत्तर दें।

मासिक व्यय मद (पाई-चार्ट शेयर)
व्यय मद | प्रतिशत शेयर (%) | केंद्रीय कोण (डिग्री)
भोजन | 40% | 144°
किराया | 25% | 90°
शिक्षा | 15% | 54°
बचत | 10% | 36°
विविध | 10% | 36°

Q. भोजन के लिए केंद्रीय कोण का बचत के लिए केंद्रीय कोण से अनुपात क्या है?
explanation_hi: भोजन के लिए केंद्रीय कोण = 144°, और बचत के लिए = 36°। अनुपात = 144 / 36 = 4 / 1 = 4 : 1 (या समतुल्य रूप से, प्रतिशत का अनुपात 40% : 10% = 4 : 1)। विकल्प C गलत है।

question:

Expenditure Head | Percentage Share (%) | Central Angle (Degrees)
Food | 40% | 144°
Rent | 25% | 90°
Education | 15% | 54°
Savings | 10% | 36°
Miscellaneous | 10% | 36°

Q. What is the difference between the central angles corresponding to Food and the sum of Savings and Miscellaneous combined?
explanation: Central angle for Food = 144°. Combined percentage of Savings and Miscellaneous = 10% + 10% = 20%, which corresponds to a central angle of 36° + 36° = 72°. Difference = 144° - 72° = 72°. Option B is incorrect arithmetic.

Q. भोजन और संयुक्त रूप से बचत तथा विविध के योग के संगत केंद्रीय कोणों के बीच का अंतर क्या है?
explanation_hi: भोजन के लिए केंद्रीय कोण = 144°। बचत और विविध का संयुक्त प्रतिशत = 10% + 10% = 20%, जो 36° + 36° = 72° के केंद्रीय कोण के संगत है। अंतर = 144° - 72° = 72°। विकल्प B गलत अंकगणित है।

question:
Study the table below showing the exports and imports of a country (in ₹ crore) over six years and answer the question.

Year | Exports (₹ Cr) | Imports (₹ Cr)
2018 | 1200 | 1500
2019 | 1400 | 1600
2020 | 1300 | 1700
2021 | 1600 | 1800
2022 | 1900 | 2000
2023 | 2200 | 2300

Q. In which year was the trade deficit (Imports - Exports) the highest?
explanation: Trade deficit = Imports - Exports. For 2018: 1500-1200=300; 2019: 1600-1400=200; 2020: 1700-1300=400; 2021: 1800-1600=200; 2022: 2000-1900=100; 2023: 2300-2200=100. Thus, the highest trade deficit is ₹400 crore in 2020. Option A (300) is incorrect as it is lower than 400.

question:
Study the table below showing the exports and imports of a country (in ₹ crore) over six years and answer the question.

Year | Exports (₹ Cr) | Imports (₹ Cr)
2018 | 1200 | 1500
2019 | 1400 | 1600
2020 | 1300 | 1700
2021 | 1600 | 1800
2022 | 1900 | 2000
2023 | 2200 | 2300

Q. What is the ratio of the total imports over the six years to the total exports over the six years?
explanation: Total Imports = 1500 + 1600 + 1700 + 1800 + 2000 + 2300 = 10900. Total Exports = 1200 + 1400 + 1300 + 1600 + 1900 + 2200 = 9600. Ratio of Imports to Exports = 10900 : 9600 = 109 : 96. Option A reverses the order incorrectly.
